module12A: Correct IAM evaluation: an explicit allow must also satisfy all applicable limits (permissions boundary, session policy, Organizations SCP/RCP). Explicit deny overrides allow; identity-based allow alone is insufficient. Label simplified example assumes no other grants and all relevant limits permit access. Preserve teaching depth and examples.

Relabel identity panel 'Policy attachment targets: users, groups, roles'. Add clearly 'Groups organize users and receive policies; groups are not request principals.' Preserve JSON and all other examples.

Fix lifecycle explanation: lifecycle transitions storage classes or expires objects; it never moves/renames object keys or prefixes. Bottom example exact: 'Lifecycle transitions older backups to archival storage classes without changing object keys. Copy objects separately to reorganize prefixes.' Preserve prefix visuals and depth.
Correct general-purpose S3 bucket shared namespace uniqueness to 'Unique across accounts and Regions within an AWS partition'. Preserve AWS partition/global region teaching and rest of slide.

Correct diagram labeling: 's3://example-bucket/datasets/train.csv' is the S3 URI. Bucket name 'example-bucket'; object key 'datasets/train.csv'; prefix 'datasets/'; basename 'train.csv'. Slashes are delimiters, not folders. Console inside datasets/ displays train.csv. Keep CSV example and rich style.

Correct storage overview: Intelligent-Tiering automatic frequent, infrequent and archive instant tiers have millisecond access; optional Archive Access and Deep Archive Access require asynchronous restore. S3 Lifecycle uses configured age/date rules, not access frequency; Intelligent-Tiering monitors access. Preserve all storage categories and comparisons.

Correct decision example: choose Standard-IA for infrequent access needing millisecond reads. Choose One Zone-IA only for recreatable data that can tolerate loss of one AZ. Archive classes depend on retrieval-time needs. Preserve existing comparison and examples.

Qualify blanket Glacier latency statement: Glacier Instant Retrieval provides millisecond reads; Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive require restore with minutes-to-hours or hours retrieval. Preserve other storage class comparisons.

Add minimum storage duration billing: 30 days for Standard-IA and One Zone-IA. Clearly distinguish One Zone-IA single-AZ resilience and recreatable data. Preserve all other accurate text and examples.

Correct exact minimum storage duration billing: Glacier Instant Retrieval 90 days; Glacier Flexible Retrieval 90 days; Glacier Deep Archive 180 days. Retrieval: Instant milliseconds; Flexible expedited 1–5 minutes (subject to capacity), standard 3–5 hours, bulk 5–12 hours; Deep standard about 12 hours, bulk about 48 hours. Explain per-GB retrieval charges. Preserve comparison architecture.

Repair Intelligent-Tiering tier diagram to show FIVE tiers: Frequent Access automatic initially; Infrequent Access automatic after 30 consecutive days no access; Archive Instant Access automatic after 90 days no access; OPTIONAL Archive Access configured from 90 days; OPTIONAL Deep Archive Access configured from 180 days. First three millisecond access; optional two require restore. Objects under 128 KB not auto-tiered, remain Frequent, no monitoring fee. Optional Archive Access can bypass Archive Instant. Preserve detailed example, glossy depth and legibility.

Qualify all Intelligent-Tiering latency claims: automatic three tiers give millisecond access; optional Archive Access and Deep Archive Access require asynchronous restore. Preserve all other storage class table content and examples.

Add accurate EC2 user data behavior: Linux user data scripts run at first launch by default; configure explicitly if repeat execution is required. Correct typo 'configuredj' to 'configured'. Keep code and worked example readable.

Repair architecture boundaries: Amazon Bedrock is AWS-managed OUTSIDE customer VPC. Put Bedrock Runtime INTERFACE ENDPOINT ENI inside private subnet, connecting to outside Bedrock through PrivateLink. Public route table belongs public subnet; private subnet route to NAT only where internet egress needed. S3 GATEWAY endpoint is a route-table association, not a subnet-hosted service. Preserve detailed two-AZ network, security groups, route tables, worked example.

Correct private route table: do not show a route with target 'none'. Remove 0.0.0.0/0 row when no internet default route; state no internet default route configured. Public subnet internet access also requires public IPv4 or IPv6, IGW route and permitted security controls. Preserve route tables and detailed architecture.

Correct endpoint diagram: Bedrock managed service OUTSIDE VPC boundary; interface endpoint ENIs inside private subnets connect via PrivateLink. Gateway endpoints support S3 and DynamoDB and are route-table associations. Keep original interface versus gateway comparison, examples and glossy architecture depth.

Correct identities: IAM users and roles can be request principals; groups organize users and receive policies but are not request principals. AWS STS issues temporary role-session credentials. Preserve all accurate authentication/authorization content and example.

Change 'six-way' to 'seven-way' if seven services shown. Fix CloudTrail relationship: API requests go to AWS services; CloudTrail OBSERVES and records supported activity via a side branch, it is not an inline authorization proxy. Preserve service comparisons and examples.

Correct SSE-KMS flow: S3 decrypts authorized GET object data server-side using KMS; returns object plaintext protected by TLS, not still-encrypted object data to application.
